newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Client forex sales boost Bulgaria lev at close.
newsitem.headline: Client forex sales boost Bulgaria lev at close.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 976-978 per mark, firmer from the opening's 978-980 due to active foreign currency sales from final clients ahead of tax and salary payments due by end-month, dealers said.

* The lev gained to 1,680-1,684 per dollar at the close from midday's 1,685-1,688 and the morning's 1,692-1,695, tracking the dollar slip against the mark on international markets and adjusting to the lev/mark.
* The mark is to become an anchor in an IMF-prescribed currency board system, to be launched from July 1, at a fixed exchange rate of 1,000 levs.

* Foreign currency demand from banks was low throughout the day despite falling yields on government securities because most banks have already built up forex positions in preparation for the currency board peg.
* A new, lower central bank main interest rate of effective annual 16.30 percent calculated through accumulation of monthly accruals took effect on Monday, down from 42.24 percent.

* The average yield to maturity on four-week discount T-bills, auctioned daily by the Finance Ministry, fell to 0.58 percent at Friday's auction from 0.62 percent on Thursday, 0.69 percent on Wednesday and 0.72 percent on Tuesday.
